transcript.text: How is everybody doing? Welcome back to another Dragon Wilds video. In this video, I'm going to go over the new
upgrade system with the Mystic Forge and the Ascension cores. I'm going to go over how all this works and just give
you guys a breakdown of it. It's pretty simple, pretty straight to the point. One thing I do want to preface with is
So, with the Ascension core system and the Mystic Forge, these can be used to upgrade Masterwork and Vestige weapons
to higher tiers using the relevant cores. For example, any weapon or gear set that is made out of any ore type
will not be able to be upgraded. Like as you can see, I have the Adamant warhammer. I cannot actually upgrade
this as well as the bronze warhammer, you cannot upgrade this. Now, to access the upgrade menu for the Mystic Forge,
you're just going to go over to the Mystic Forge here. And you're going to see that you have crafting, repairing,
and then there is a new menu option right here, and this is Ascension upgrades. Upgrade the power level of
Masterwork weapons and armor. So, any Masterwork item and any Vestige item. So, any base recipe item or any armor
weapon made out of ore cannot be upgraded, so keep that in mind. I do want to quickly preface that power level
seven shards do not exist in the world yet. The recipe to convert power level seven shards to cores does exist in the
Mystic Forge. This is not intentional, it's currently a bug with this update, and they will be removing the recipe
with the 1.0 update. The only way to obtain power level seven cores is from the Nightmare Crucible directly and not
through converting shards, so keep that in mind. So, instead of using these Ascension shards to then create a core,
when it comes to tier seven, you cannot actually do that. You have to just find the core itself, which only drops from
the Nightmare Crucible. If you guys haven't already, go farm the Nightmare Crucible, farm it up, get some tier
seven cores cuz that's the only way currently you can obtain that resource. Briefly to go over how this works is
you're going to have your Ascension cores. Now, in order to make Ascension cores, you do need Ascension shards, and
you're going to need 99 of them. If you go to the bottom section of the Mystic Forge to Ascension cores right here, you
guys are going to see that you're going to need 99 of that specific shard in order to craft one core, plus other
materials as well. As you guys can see, it costs one core to level up an item. So, Ascension Core 4, you're going to be
leveling up an item from level three to four, and then five will be four to five, and then six will be five to six.
Now, I'm going to give you guys a few examples here. So, you guys will now notice on your items, they will either
have a purple hue or a gold hue on it. And that simply means gold is masterwork weapons, and purple are Visage items.
There's no other indication on that. That's just simply what they are. These are just Visage items in standard
recipes, and then the purple items are actually masterwork. So, I'm going to give you a few examples. We're going to
start with the highest level one-handed weapon in the new region of Umbral Sands. This is power level seven, and
this is the Toxzil Och. This weapon at its base does 93 to 168 damage. So, we are going to take the Chieftain's Blade,
which is a power level three. As you can see, it only does 29 to 52 damage. In order to upgrade this, we're going to
need a core for each level. So, to get it to a tier four, you're going to need a tier four core. The five, a tier five
core, so on and so forth. Now, there's two ways you can actually do this. I'm going to show you guys both ways. I'm
going to drop these on the ground. So, we have the tier four. We're going to go from three to four. We're going to go
over here to our menu, and you're just going to throw this into the Mystic Forge like you would any other piece of
equipment. We're going to put it in there, and as you can see, Ascension Core 4. We're going to go from power
level three to four. Boom. So, as you can see, there's a new symbol above this weapon now, and that's just an up arrow.
And that's just an indication that you have increased the power level of that weapon. That's simply what the arrow
means. Now, there is another way you can do this. We're going to pick up all of these. As you guys see, we have Let me
rearrange this so it's easier to see. So, now we have Ascension Core 5, 6, and 7 in our inventory. This is tier four.
So, if you have all the Ascension Cores you want in your inventory, and you go to the Mystic Forge, and you put the
item in it, so this is tier four. We're going to ascend it, and it's going to burn up all your Ascension Cores to get
it to the highest tier possible, depending on the Cores that you have in your inventory. We just went from four
to seven. Now, as you guys can see, there's a new symbol above this item, and you can see my abyssal whip has the
same thing. The star is an indication that that level is currently at the highest power level that the game
offers. So, that's simply what the star means. It's easy and straightforward. So, now you can see the toxic staff does
93 to 168 base damage, and now this weapon does 90 to 162. Keep in mind, different gear sets and different
weapons, they are going to scale to the current power level. Some of them will do more damage than a current tier seven
weapon, while others might not. So, for instance, the Chieftain's blade technically does less damage than the
base power level seven item that you can find in Umbral Sands. But, here's another example. Going to go over to the
staff now. The Pharaoh's staff is a power level seven item that you find in Umbral Sands. The staff of light is a
fan favorite, is a power level four. Staff of light does 4.5 damage, whereas the Pharaoh's staff does 8.4. Watch what
happens when I upgrade this to the highest tier. So, as you can see, we have the staff of light tier four. We
have an ascension core four, five, six, and seven. We're going to go into our mystic forge. We're going to pop the
staff of light here, and it's going to burn up all of our ascension cores. Now, it has a star indicating that it's the
highest power level. And like I said, the Chieftain's blade is at the highest power level, it technically does not do
more damage, but now the staff of light does more damage than the Pharaoh's staff. The Pharaoh's staff has a special
action to it, but at its base it does 8.4 rune damage, and now the staff of light does 8.7. So, keep that in mind.
With gear, with weapons, it depends on the scaling based off of what the piece of gear's basic stats were when you
first started upgrading it. Now, we're going to upgrade the Paladin's plate body. This is a tier four item. As you
can see, it does plus 30 melee defense, plus 25 range defense, plus 23 magic defense. We're going to compare it to
the obsidian chestplate that does 53, 47, and 45. Let's go tier this up. Again, we have ascension core five, six,
and seven, so we're just going to burn all of those up in one go, and now it has a star on it, and it indicates to us
that it's at the highest power level the game offers. Now, let's compare the stats to the obsidian set. They're 100%
the same now, which is great. So, weapons are going to vary based off of their basic stats to start. But when it
comes to armor pieces, they are going to scale and completely match the highest tier item that the game offer. Keep that
in mind, which is very good because now we basically can wear any set we want, which I really like cuz there's a lot of
sets that are older that I really enjoy. And guys, look at this, the abyssal whip tier seven. Come on, give me a break.
Everybody loves this weapon. I think these are the two biggest fan favorites for the game, the abyssal whip as well
as the staff of light. So, now they're up there. Now we can use them. I'm going to be using both of those because the
Pharaoh staff technically does less damage. Yes, we do have the sworn servant, but that thing's bugged
anyways, no pun intended. So, this is a quick guide on Ascension Course. Let me know down in the comments below if you
guys have any more questions. I tried to break it down as best as I could for you guys, and I tried my best to go into a
ton of detail. I know this video might be long, but I really wanted to break it down. Again, if you guys have any more
questions or concerns, let me know down in the comments below. I will definitely help you guys out. If this video is out
on Sythone, please drop a like on it and subscribe for all things Dragon Waltz. Everything survival crafting, that's
what we do here. We'd love to have you. And as always guys, stay happy, stay hyped, and have a beautiful day.

comments.author: @Dragonrumpus
comments.text:
The Masterwork upgrades for weapons & armour has been slowly building hype since Fellhollow when our OG Masterworks got outclassed by the new tier

Jagex mentioned Masterwork upgrades for tools will come in future, which is great because I love my Undead Spade & it's sad I have to swap to adamant to clear my new yew plots; but also interesting since afaik that's the only Masterwork tool so far

I do still hope we get our jewelry slot split into an amulet & ring slot; & that we might one day get "Social" slots like Terraria does where we can have one set of actual armour on & another one for looks (I found that Necromancer's Crown with Dragonkin Mage legs & Dark Mage top looks GREAT together, but Dark Mage isn't Masterwork & thus can't be upgraded), if it includes capes then we could equip one with an affect on it, like the Zamorak Cape, & have a different one in Social

And with the devs saying that due to Masterwork upgrades ascending old gear to be on equal footing, they're looking into more unique effects for different sets; then there's a potential high future value in doing OSRS style mix & matching of gear from different sets for their effects, & RS style of slapping a different set on top for looks!
